problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}10 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices given above.
Find an orthogonal matrix $P$ such that $x=Py$ defines the corresponding change of variables that reduces the quadratic form $Q(x)={x}^{T}\,Ax$ to the canonical (diagonal) form ${y}^{T}\,Dy.$
worked_solution:
Every quadratic form can be reduced to its canonical (diagonal) form using orthogonal transformations.

From the diagonal matrix $D,$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ are 

$\,$ ${\lambda }_{1}=10,\,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=5,\,$ and $\,{\lambda }_{3}=3.$

Now, we need to find an eigenvector basis of $A.$ 

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=10,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-10I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-10[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-10I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{1}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{1}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-5I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-5I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{2}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{2}‖=\sqrt{5},$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

- For ${\lambda }_{3}=3,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 9 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Seeking a non-zero solution of $(A-3I)x=0$ gives the eigenvector ${v}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Dividing ${v}_{3}$ by its norm $‖{v}_{3}‖=1,$ we get 

$$
\frac{{v}_{3}}{‖{v}_{3}‖}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, we construct the orthogonal matrix $P$ in the usual way, and this gives us the following:

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0\end{aligned}]
$$
